pr_title: planner: do not use like to build range when new collation is enabled

### What problem does this PR solve?
<!--

Please create an issue first to describe the problem.

There MUST be one line starting with "Issue Number:  " and 
linking the relevant issues via the "close" or "ref".

For more info, check https://pingcap.github.io/tidb-dev-guide/contribute-to-tidb/contribute-code.html#referring-to-an-issue.

-->

Issue Number: close https://github.com/pingcap/tidb/issues/31174

Problem Summary:
The like condition will be used to build range, but it can not handle some situations.

### What is changed and how it works?
You can see [here](https://github.com/pingcap/tidb/issues/31174) for more details. But in this PR, we only forbid using the like condition to build range when new collation is enabled and the column type is non-binary collation string.

issue_context.title: `LIKE` does not work as expected for utf8_general_ci strings
issue_context.body:
## Bug Report

Please answer these questions before submitting your issue. Thanks!

### 1. Minimal reproduce step (Required)

```sql
drop table if exists t;
create table t(a char(4) collate utf8_general_ci primary key /*T![clustered_index] clustered */);
insert into t values("`?");
explain select * from t where a like "`%";
select * from t where a like "`%";
```

<!-- a step by step guide for reproducing the bug. -->

### 2. What did you expect to see? (Required)

```console
+----+
| a  |
+----+
| `? |
+----+
```

### 3. What did you see instead (Required)

```sql
mysql> explain select * from t where a like "`%";
+-------------+---------+------+---------------+---------------+
| id          | estRows | task | access object | operator info |
+-------------+---------+------+---------------+---------------+
| TableDual_5 | 0.00    | root |               | rows:0        |
+-------------+---------+------+---------------+---------------+
1 row in set (0.00 sec)

mysql> select * from t where a like "`%";
Empty set (0.01 sec)
```

### 4. What is your TiDB version? (Required)

<!-- Paste the output of SELECT tidb_version() -->
8a83d01ac
comments:
The root cause is the incorrect way to build range for pattern matching `%` in `LIKE`:

https://github.com/pingcap/tidb/blob/321d307f3b23877fb2be0e7534a9ecd6a655be05/util/ranger/points.go#L688-L705

This algorithm constructs the range in byte-level: for example, `ab%` is mapped to `[ab, ac]` by adding `1` to the last byte. However, this is incorrect for non-binary collation strings because the **sort key order** is not the same as **byte order**.

In this issue,  `` `% `` is mapped to the range `` [`, a] ``(where `` ` `` is `0x60` and `a` is `0x61`). Because the collation `utf8_general_ci` is case-insensitive, `a` and `A` have the same sort key. Finally, the range comes to be `` [`, A] ``, which is actually an empty range.

The reproduce conditions:
1. The `LIKE` operator is used. 
1. Pattern match syntax `%` is used.
1. The column type is non-binary collation string.
1. A boundary char of 2 ranges like "`" is used.

@aytrack Since this is a corner case bug, I prefer not to tag it with "severity/critical".
degree to major since the 4th condition is a corner case.
Please check whether the issue should be labeled with 'affects-x.y' or 'fixes-x.y.z', and then remove 'needs-more-info' label.

review_comments: When `collation == "binary"`, it is OK use use the range built by `LIKE`.
